title: Schorseneren (Salsify)

Scrape them in small pieces at a time and immediately place these in cold, boiled water or water with a splash of milk or vinegar to keep the color white.
Wash them and cook them until tender in abundant boiling water with milk and salt (30 minutes).

Let them drain in a colander and stew them for 5 minutes in the sauce of butter or margarine, flour and milk prepared in the same way as cauliflower sauce (see recipe 328) or cornstarch sauce (see recipe 329).
Grate some nutmeg over them in the bowl.

title: Schuimige Aardbeienpudding (Fluffy Strawberry Pudding)
description: A pudding made with strawberries, juice, and brown sugar.

ingredients.name: 17 1/2 g gelatine with 1/2 sheet red gelatine, or 12 1/2 g powdered gelatine

steps: Pick the strawberries, wash them, select the finest ones to place whole in the pudding later and set them aside sprinkled with some sugar for a time.
Press the remaining strawberries through a horsehair sieve.
Soak the sheet gelatine 10 to 15 minutes in cold water.
Dissolve it with the sugar in a little boiling water (see instructions page 267, 5°).
Let this solution cool.
Stir it into the strawberry purée.
Add the sieved lemon juice.
Fold the mixture through the stiffly beaten cream and the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Mix with the reserved strawberries.
Stir the mass from time to time.
When the mixture becomes jelly-like, pour it into a pudding mold brushed with unbeaten egg white.
Let the pudding become cold and firm, turn it out onto a damp plate and serve without sauce, but garnish the pudding if desired with Rhine wine jelly and some strawberries.

title: Schuimige Vanillepudding (Fluffy Vanilla Pudding)
description: A pudding made with whipped cream, vanilla or sugar, and gelatine.

ingredients.name: 14 g gelatine or 12 g powdered gelatine

steps: Beat the egg yolks vigorously with a spoonful of sugar.
Rinse the pudding mold with unbeaten egg white and set it upside down to let the excess egg white run out and keep the mold from drying out.

Bring the milk slowly to a boil with the split vanilla stick and the remaining sugar, pour it, stirring vigorously, into the beaten yolks, put everything back in the pan and let the mixture, beating with a whisk, be bound over the fire (but especially do not boil).
Dissolve the sheet gelatine, after soaking 10 to 15 minutes in cold water, in the hot liquid, which has been taken from the fire.
Remove the vanilla.
Let the mass cool briefly.
Beat the cream and the egg whites stiff, pour in the pudding mixture while stirring and let it stand, stirring from time to time, until it begins to become jelly-like.
Then pour it into the pudding mold and let the pudding become cold and firm.

title: Spekkoek (Layered Spice Cake)
description: A cake made with butter or margarine, sugar, and flour.
steps: Stir the butter or margarine until creamy, add the sugar and egg yolks and stir until the sugar is well ground.
Add the spices and sifted flour.
Beat the egg white as stiffly as possible, fold in the remaining mixture.
Grease a cake pan with butter or margarine, spread a layer of batter as thinly as possible and bake in a moderately warm oven until light brown.
Brush with melted butter or margarine, spread a second layer and bake until light brown as well.
Continue until all the batter is baked, turn the cake out onto a cake rack and let it cool.
Dust with powdered sugar and cut into very thin slices.

Note: While baking, keep the remaining batter as cool as possible so the egg white does not collapse. If making a large cake, the spices can be stirred through one half of the dough while the other half remains white, making the separation between layers more visible. This cake can be stored for a long time in a tin.

Fry the pancake on both sides until light brown and cooked through

title: Tulband (Bread Dough Ring Cake)

steps: Place flour in a warmed bowl, make a well in the center, add yeast, half the milk warmed to lukewarm and half a teaspoon sugar

Bake in a fairly warm oven until light brown and cooked through (½ hour to ¾ hour)

description: A bread preparation made with yeast, flour, and salt.

title: Zakeieren (Poached Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, vinegar, and water.
steps: Use the freshest possible eggs for this
Bring water to a boil in a wide pan, add some salt and a small splash of vinegar
Break the eggs as close as possible above the water surface, or break them first into a cup and let them slide into the water
Quickly wrap the white, which immediately begins to set, around the yolk using two spoons and let the eggs simmer gently for 3 minutes
Remove them from the pan with a skimming spoon and cut or trim off the loose flakes of white
Lay them on pieces of toasted bread or bread fried in butter or margarine, in a bowl of very strong broth for soup, or serve them with tomato, béchamel, curry sauce etc.
